children: Fairfax's investment arm acquired 4.4 crore shares from IIFL Capital Services promoters, while separately offloading a 13.24 per cent holding in IIFL Finance for Rs 3,488 crore

Fairfax Financial Holdings' investment vehicle FIH Mauritius Investments has reshaped its holdings in two IIFL Group companies through transactions worth a combined Rs 5,028 crore, buying an 11.8 per cent stake in IIFL Capital Services while exiting a substantial holding in IIFL Finance.

In the latest transaction on Thursday, FIH Mauritius acquired 4.4 crore shares of IIFL Capital Services at Rs 350 apiece, taking an 11.8 per cent stake in the company. The purchase, valued at Rs 1,540 crore, was matched by share disposals from the company's promoter group through bulk deals on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The largest portion of the shares came from promoter Nirmal Bhanwarlal Jain, who sold 3.23 crore shares for Rs 1,130.5 crore. Venkataraman Rajamani, another promoter, transferred 87 lakh shares valued at Rs 304.5 crore. Their respective disposals represented 8.7 per cent and 2.3 per cent of IIFL Capital Services.

The remaining 30 lakh shares were sold by promoter group entities Ardent Impex and Kalki Family Private Trust. The former offloaded 20 lakh shares worth Rs 70 crore, while the trust sold 10 lakh shares for Rs 35 crore.

The transactions follow changes to the investment agreement originally signed on May 7, 2026. IIFL Capital Services disclosed on November 18 that it had entered into an amendment agreement with FIH Mauritius, Jain and Rajamani, allowing the secondary share transfers to be completed through market or off-market transactions.

Ardent Impex and Kalki Family Private Trust subsequently signed deeds of adherence to the agreement, formally bringing their combined 30 lakh-share sale to FIH Mauritius under the same terms and conditions as the original arrangement.

The 30 September 2026 shareholding disclosures showed that Jain owned 12.60 per cent of IIFL Capital Services, while Rajamani held 3 per cent. Kalki Family Private Trust, whose trustee is Aditi Avinash Athavankar, had a 2.41 per cent holding, and Ardent Impex owned 0.72 per cent.
Despite the stake acquisition, IIFL Capital Services shares ended Thursday's trading at Rs 334.70 on the BSE, down 5.10 per cent from the previous close of Rs 352.70.

In another disclosure, the company said SES ESG Research or (SES ESG Ratings) had voluntarily assigned it an environmental, social and governance (ESG) score of 75.4, drawing on its FY26 disclosures and other publicly available information.
Fairfax Also Exits IIFL Finance Holding

The IIFL Capital Services transaction follows a much larger divestment by FIH Mauritius in another group company. On 18 November, the Fairfax investment arm sold 5.65 crore shares of IIFL Finance, representing approximately 13.24 per cent of the non-banking financial company, in block and bulk deals.

The shares changed hands at Rs 617 apiece, taking the total transaction value to Rs 3,488 crore, according to BSE data. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas were among the institutional investors that purchased shares in the transaction.
IIFL Finance's exchange disclosures showed that FIH Mauritius held 5,82,13,166 shares, equivalent to a 13.64 per cent stake, at the end of September 2026.

Taken together, the two transactions mark a significant change in FIH Mauritius' investments across the IIFL group, with the investor reducing its exposure to IIFL Finance while acquiring a substantial holding in IIFL Capital Services.
